findings.problem: nativeHeadIdentityMatches compares identity.supporting against a boolean check, but then strictly checks appearance.supportingModel === actor. For principal actors ('lila' and 'karo'), identity.supporting is false, but if appearance.supportingModel is defined on a principal character or omitted inconsistently, it checks appearance.supportingModel === undefined. More critically, in host schemas, HostProfileSchema.appearance validates `!nativeHeadIdentityMatches(a, a.bodyHeadBank.actor)`. For supporting models, `appearance.characterVariant` is matched against `identity.bodyTemplate`, but `nativeHeadIdentities['prehistoric-male-bald'].bodyTemplate` is 'karo'. When matching, `nativeHeadIdentityMatches` checks `appearance.characterVariant === identity.bodyTemplate && (identity.supporting ? appearance.supportingModel === actor : appearance.supportingModel === undefined)`. However, if `appearance.characterVariant` is undefined (which is optional on `HostProfileSchema.appearance`), `appearance.characterVariant === identity.bodyTemplate` fails even if `supportingModel` is validly configured.
findings.repair: Ensure characterVariant is populated or resolve bodyTemplate via prehistoricSupportingModel when matching supporting identities if characterVariant is optional on the input appearance object.

findings.problem: When validating NativeHeadBankDefinitionSchema, bank-4 or bank-3 multi-source banks allow `c.face.mouth.rest.sourceId`. The check `const usedSources=new Set([...b.cells.map(sourceId),...b.cells.flatMap(c=>c.face?.mouth.rest?[c.face.mouth.rest.sourceId]:[])]);` collects string IDs, but `sourceId` helper returns `undefined` for multi-source cells where `c.sourceId` is undefined before `c.sourceId` presence is validated, adding `undefined` to `usedSources`. Furthermore, `sources.some(s=>!usedSources.has(s.id))` compares `s.id` against `usedSources`. If a cell uses `source.id` but `b.source` has id `'primary'`, cells in bank 4 with `sourceId: 'primary'` are permitted, but `NativeHeadSourceFileSchema` requires files matching `/^library\/topics\/prehistoric-life\/(?:head-turn-studies\/(?:lila|karo)-head-turn-v[1-9]\d*|(?:head-cells|head-face-plates)\/(?:lila|karo|prehistoric-male-bald|prehistoric-female-haired)-head-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}-v[1-9]\d*)\.png$(?![\s\S])/`. However, for supporting models, `b.primary` in `nativeHeadIdentities` is `docs/topics/assets/reference-...` which is validated against `readSource`. In `readSource`: `if(!NativeHeadSourceFileSchema.safeParse(file).success&&!Object.values(nativeHeadIdentities).some(identity=>identity.primary.file===file))throw new Error(...)`. In `nativeHeadResources`, `b.source.file` is validated by `readNativeHeadSource(root, source, bank.primary)` which calls `readSource(root, source.file)`. This works, but in `NativeHeadBankDefinitionSchema`, `b.primary.file` is not checked against `NativeHeadSourceFileSchema` only `b.source.file`. But if `b.actor` has a bank-4 registration where `b.source.file` is in `head-cells/`, `!s.file.split('/').at(-1)!.startsWith(b.actor+'-head-')` checks that the file starts with `b.actor+'-head-'`. For supporting models `b.actor` is `'prehistoric-male-bald'` or `'prehistoric-female-haired'`. If a closed-mouth plate is included in `additionalSources`, its file must also start with `${b.actor}-head-`, which matches the regex.
findings.sourceEvidence: if(!s.file.split('/').at(-1)!.startsWith(b.actor+'-head-'))fail('Head bank source and identity must belong to the same actor');
findings.repair: Ensure tests verify that closed-mouth plate filename prefixes strictly follow `${b.actor}-head-` format rather than generic plates.

findings.problem: In `supportingNativeTopicAppearance`, `supportingTopicAppearance(a.supportingModel)` is called, which calls `topicAppearance(...)` and returns `{ characterVariant: bodyTemplate, supportingModel: model, ... }`. Then `supportingNativeTopicAppearance` sets `{...supportingTopicAppearance(a.supportingModel), artworkVersion:'forest-body-view-1', bodyView:a.bodyView, bodyHeadBank:a.bodyHeadBank, ...}`. But `topicAppearance` sets `artworkVersion: 'forest-body-1'`, which gets overridden to `'forest-body-view-1'`. However, in `applyTopicCast`, the assignment for principal is `character.appearance = principal ? topicAppearance(character.id as 'lila'|'karo') : requested.artworkVersion==='forest-body-view-1'||requested.bodyHeadBank||requested.bodyView ? supportingNativeTopicAppearance(requested) : supportingTopicAppearance(requested.supportingModel!)`. But if `character.appearance` was updated, `character.costume` is deleted (`delete character.costume;`). Notice that in `topicAppearance`, `characterVariant` is set to `id` ('lila' or 'karo'). However, in `HostProfileSchema`, `a.characterVariant` is optional. In `applyTopicCast`, `supportingNativeTopicAppearance` parses `input` with `HostProfileSchema.shape.appearance.parse(input)`. In `HostProfileSchema`, the refine check requires: `if(a.artworkVersion==='forest-body-view-1'&&(!a.bodyView||!a.characterVariant))ctx.addIssue(...)`. If the input story actor has `supportingModel` and `artworkVersion: 'forest-body-view-1'` but omitted `characterVariant` (expecting it to be inferred from `supportingModel`), `HostProfileSchema.shape.appearance.parse(input)` will throw a validation error before `supportingTopicAppearance` has a chance to supply `characterVariant: prehistoricSupportingModel(model).bodyTemplate`.
findings.repair: Ensure `characterVariant` matching `prehistoricSupportingModel(input.supportingModel).bodyTemplate` is populated on `input` prior to parsing with `HostProfileSchema.shape.appearance.parse(input)`, or relax the requirement that callers must explicitly declare `characterVariant` when `supportingModel` is already explicitly specified.
